content.jointProblem: Investigate where Serbian Cyrillic–Latin normalization should occur in KlozuraPro’s PostgreSQL search pipeline to reduce script-related missed contracts without introducing false matches or unacceptable latency. The first experiment would compare indexing-time, query-time and combined normalization against the current baseline on an approved, annotated contract/query sample covering mixed scripts and ambiguous Latin sequences, measuring retrieval precision, recall, zero-hit rate, indexing overhead and p95 query latency.

rationale.text: Papp has directly relevant research on script normalization before indexing Serbian news from sources using different scripts.

sources.quote: Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja.

rationale.text: Her search research explicitly measures normalization overhead, providing a useful starting point for performance-aware experiments rather than assuming normalization is free.

sources.quote: Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije.

rationale.text: She has experience constructing annotated evaluation data for legal texts involving Serbian, relevant to designing a contract-search test set.

sources.quote: We constructed a manually annotated corpus of 4,200 sentence pairs extracted from EU directive translations and national legislative texts.

rationale.text: She has completed an applied document-matching engagement with an internally deployed prototype, supporting the practical collaboration format.

sources.quote: The engagement resulted in a prototype system deployed internally by the company.

constraints.text: The intervention must integrate with the existing PostgreSQL full-text search pipeline; choosing indexing-time, query-time or combined normalization is part of the work.

sources.quote: our full-text search index in PostgreSQL treats the two scripts as completely different character sets.
at indexing time, at query time, or both

constraints.text: Correctness testing must cover mixed-script documents and ambiguous Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings, not only uniformly written documents.

sources.quote: robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones
the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions.

constraints.text: Search responsiveness is a hard acceptance condition; the company must quantify what counts as a noticeable slowdown before implementation.

sources.quote: does not slow down search response times noticeably.

constraints.text: Scope must fit the task-specific allocation of one backend engineer for at most six weeks and the company's one-external-project capacity.

sources.quote: We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks.
capacity for roughly one external project at a time alongside normal product development.

constraints.text: Scheduling must respect the researcher's stated teaching-load restriction; the recorded earliest start does not establish current availability.

sources.quote: Papp is currently at full teaching load and can take on new projects only from late 2025 onward.

risks: The closest search evidence concerns Serbian news-stream indexing, not contract retrieval in PostgreSQL. Its indexing-overhead result does not establish query latency or legal-term correctness; the first experiment must test this transfer explicitly.
Normalization may conflate distinct terms or names, while ambiguous mappings may still miss relevant contracts. Recall gains must be checked against false matches.
The reported one-in-five failure estimate comes from January 2024 logs and may not represent current traffic or isolate script mismatch from other retrieval problems.

Access to representative contracts, query logs and relevance annotations is unknown. Confidentiality restrictions could prevent realistic evaluation unless an approved data-access arrangement is established.
Current researcher availability, project budget and alignment with the six-week engineering window remain unknown.
questions: Can Papp confirm current availability and time commitment for a joint project, and can that overlap with the backend engineer's six-week window?
What budget, start date and deliverables are approved, including ownership of implementation, testing and production rollout?

Can the company provide approved contract text, query logs and relevance judgments covering both scripts, mixed-script documents and ambiguous sequences? Who will annotate them, and under what access and confidentiality rules?
What are the current PostgreSQL version, text-search configuration, tokenization and stemming rules, index size, document volume and query load?
What numerical limits apply to p95 query latency, indexing overhead and storage growth, and what precision/recall trade-off is acceptable?
Can the January 2024 estimate be rechecked on current logs, and which concrete ambiguous mappings, names or legal terms must the first experiment include?
What reindexing window, staging environment and rollback process are available?
